pages.text: "I'll feed the baby!" Nils the little bear scurried to the box by the stove. The fallen chick cheeped inside. Nils grabbed it in his paw.
"Big brother will feed you. Stay still!" Nils gripped tight and pushed soft bread into its beak. The chick fluttered and turned its head away.
Bread fell to the box floor. The chick shut its beak tight. "Why won't you eat? I'm giving it to you!" His voice rose. The chick hid in a corner.
Grandpa Bruno approached, dusting his vest. "Open your paw." Nils opened it. The bread was crushed flat.
Grandpa spread his broad palm, five fingers in a row. Gently placed on it, the chick sat still. "Don't grab. Let the baby sit like this."
Grandpa offered bread before the beak and waited still. The chick stretched its head out and pecked, taking it itself. Grandpa said softly, "Before the beak, gently!"
Nils opened his paw wide too. No tight fist. He gently held bread before the beak and held his breath. Peck! The chick took it. "Before the beak, gently!"
One bite, two, three. The chick's neck bulged. Finished, it nestled against his paw and closed its eyes. "I didn't grab, but it didn't run away?" Nils whispered.
Nils opened his paw and counted. "One, paw open wide! Two, before the beak, gently! Three, wait until it takes a bite!" Both paws high! "Before the beak, gently!"
Grandpa stroked Nils's back with his broad palm. Grip tight, and it runs. Offer gently, and it comes itself. Nils whispered to the box, "Before the beak, gently! Sleep well, baby."
